review: Conventional NP/model nonvacuity and end-to-end encoding audit
verdict: accepted at the stated concrete-machine and designated-output-track boundary
scope: Read-only inspection of definitions, quantifiers, finite operational interfaces, decoder semantics, final endpoint composition, and targeted kernel/axiom checks. This is not a second reconstruction of every imported simulation proof. NPStackMachine and the new output-observation/determinism modules were authored by this reviewer and are not claimed as independently implementation-reviewed here.
findings: InNP quantifies one fixed finite one-tape nondeterministic machine and one natural-coefficient polynomial before universally quantifying all binary input words. Its tape starts with exactly those bits and blank elsewhere; each step selects one global finite rule and updates one cell/head/state.

Acceptance within the clock is the explicit conventional clocked-machine convention. It is not an arbitrary certificate predicate, input-dependent machine, restricted set of source machines, or promise of satisfiability. Arbitrary Machine and Polynomial witnesses are passed through CookLevin.np_to_cnf for arbitrary languages.

Kernel-checked audit examples establish that every Machine/Polynomial bounded-acceptance language satisfies InNP by definition, and both the empty language and universal language have concrete zero-clock machine witnesses. Thus the class is not empty or a single vacuous predicate.

PolynomialProgram requires a finite control type and finite collection of Boolean stacks, NoChoice on the full instruction table, and a bounded real accepting output Run for every input. PolyManyOne universally requires the exact language iff. It has no supplied runtime arithmetic or semantic callback instruction.

The numbered one-tape compiler has a finite multi-track alphabet. Its exact finite-table decoding, raw input initialization, stack-height-dependent forward simulation and all-accepting backward simulation are proved. Fixed finite table/alphabet size is a program constant, not an input-dependent unit-cost operation.

PolynomialProgram.one_tape_output now explicitly exports an actual numbered one-tape execution from raw input within clockPolynomial, accepting at head zero, with every designated output-track cell equal to the bottom-to-top encoding of f(input), including the terminal None cells.

NPPolynomialDeterministicSimulation now proves global Step uniqueness for the exact numbered compiled machine whenever the source is NoChoice. The proof handles every control/symbol pair, including initialization and unreachable microstates, by singleton local actions and injective finite rule coding. PolynomialProgram.one_tape_deterministic is the direct exported corollary; it applies to the same machine as one_tape_output.

Composition uses actual finite instruction embedding and two charged reversal transfers. Its polynomial accounts for the first output length and second-program clock. It is not semantic composition with an assumed cost counter.

PaperTheoremTwo quantifies hardness over every language satisfying InNP. Both general and fixed K=2/alpha=1 original randomized-MNL policy languages are exactly equated with the independent parsed real-feasibility source predicates.

The source decoder/legality predicate covers malformed data, declared-count consistency, positive prices/attractions/denominators, 0<alpha<=1, and 1<=K<=n, while target revenue may have either sign. Fixed parameters are numerical, retaining redundant rational and bit encodings.
No extra operational, LP, Subset Sum completeness, Cook-Levin, normalization, legal-input, or certificate-size premise remains in the exported PaperTheoremTwo NPComplete endpoints.
algorithm_boundary: Finite-state enumeration uses Classical.choice/Fintype.equivFin. These choices determine fixed finite tables; they are not runtime oracles. Some composed definitions consequently do not support direct Lean native #eval extraction without an executable enumeration refinement.

The one-tape output theorem preserves a designated encoded finite-alphabet track. No cleanup into a standalone plain binary output tape is asserted. The proof-side decodedSymbol observation is a fixed finite inverse table.
The theorem is about counted primitive transitions and their concrete-machine simulation, not measured host-language running time, compiler wall-clock time, or executable artifact performance.
